title: System Overlay
concept: A five-step order for hard conversations, so they end with who does what.
whenToUse: When you need to raise something touchy, ask for a change, make a repair or decide something together. If you start going in circles, find the step you skipped and go back to it.
steps: Warm up — say the warmest true thing you can. Remind each other you’re on the same team.
Make it safe — say out loud that the relationship isn’t at risk tonight.
Say what happened — describe it, then say how it felt and what it meant to you.
Ask for one thing — make it specific and doable, with a time to do it by.
Agree on next steps — decide who does what, by when, and when you’ll check back in.

phrases.text: I love us, and I’m not trying to fight.
When X happened, I felt Y; the impact was Z.
Can we try ___ this week and check in on ___?

working: B opens with something kind, says it isn’t a breakup talk, then: “When you scrolled while I talked, I felt dismissed and shut down.” B makes one ask: ten phone-free minutes at night. They try it for a week and check in on Friday.
notWorking: A jumps straight to a rule: “No phones at night — it’s rude.” Without warming up, making it safe, and owning A’s side first, it comes across as control, and the fight turns into “always/never.”
activity: A 12-minute practice run: pick something low-stakes, use all five steps out loud, and take turns keeping each other to the order. Aim for a little better, not perfect.
